name: Hainzenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Nestled above the Zillertal, a charming mountain village with traditional farms and breathtaking valley views.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hainzenberg is situated at an altitude of 910 metres on a sun-drenched mountain terrace in the Zillertal valley, within the district of Schwaz. Spanning roughly 21 square kilometres along the scenic ascent toward the Gerlos Pass, the mountain community is home to around 730 residents. Positioned opposite the mouth of the Gerlos valley, the village commands a magnificent panorama over the valley basin of Zell am Ziller and the Zillertal Alps. Hainzenberg is characterized by traditional mountain homesteads, idyllic alpine meadows, and fragrant coniferous forests. Both in winter and summer, the Gerlosstein cable car connects the village directly to the family-friendly Gerlosstein adventure and skiing domain, part of the extensive Zillertal Arena.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1309 under the name Haitzenperch. The name likely stems from Hoanzen, the traditional wooden drying racks once used by mountain farmers to cure hay on steep slopes. Hainzenberg achieved historic renown through its gold mining industry, first recorded in 1506. During the 17th and 18th centuries, the deposits grew into Tyrol's only substantial gold mine, sparking fierce political and legal conflicts between the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg and the counts of Tyrol. Perched on a scenic ridge stands the pilgrimage church of Maria Rast, consecrated in 1659 by a Salzburg mining administrator in gratitude for prosperous gold veins, which remains a venerated cultural treasure.

Getting There

By automobile, drivers travel via the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, then take the federal highway B169 through the valley to Zell am Ziller. Just past the town, the Gerlos Alpine Road B165 winds upward through sweeping bends to Hainzenberg. Railway passengers arrive at Jenbach station via ÖBB intercity services, transferring to the scenic Zillertalbahn railway to Zell am Ziller station. From the station square, VVT regional bus line 4094 operates regular services up to Hainzenberg, stopping directly at the Gerlossteinbahn valley station. During the winter season, a dedicated ski bus is provided free of charge.

Tips

A signature excursion is the Hainzenberg Gold Mine (Goldschaubergwerk), where guided tours lead subterranean visitors through 350 years of mining history, complete with gold panning stations. Adjacent to the mine lies the Hochzeller Käsealm, featuring an artisan cheese museum and tasting parlour alongside an animal petting zoo. Outdoor enthusiasts take the Gerlossteinbahn cable car to the mountain heights: In winter, thrill-seekers race down the 7-kilometre floodlit toboggan run, the longest in the Zillertal. In summer, the challenging Gerlossteinwand via ferrata and the Almflieger zipline delight adventure seekers, while hikers enjoy the contemplative trail to Maria Rast church.
